# jurisdiction-kit

> Zero-dependency TypeScript library providing professional body registries, data protection law details, and jurisdiction intelligence for 28 countries. Look up compliance rules, look up the recorded cross-border data transfer mechanism, find regulated professions, and rank jurisdictions by confidence score.

## What it does

jurisdiction-kit is a static, curated dataset of jurisdiction metadata — professional bodies, data protection laws, child protection rules, mutual recognition agreements, and e-signature status — exposed through a typed query API. No network requests, no external dependencies.

## Covered jurisdictions (28)

GB, US, FR, DE, ES, IT, NL, CA, AU, NZ, JP, KR, BR, MX, AR, IN, SG, AE, SA, ZA, CN, HK, IE, TR, ID, NG, KE, IL.

## Profession types

legal, medical, notary, accounting, engineering, teaching, financial, veterinary, pharmacy, architecture, social-work.

## API surface

### Data lookup

- `getJurisdiction(code)`: returns a `Jurisdiction | undefined` by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Case-insensitive. Narrow the result before use (required under `strict`).
- `getJurisdictionCodes()` — returns all available jurisdiction codes.
- `getProfessionalBodies(code, profession?)` — returns professional bodies, optionally filtered by profession type.
- `getMutualRecognitionPartners(code)`: returns jurisdictions with professional credential recognition agreements. One-directional lists; codes outside the 28 covered are dropped.
- `isProfessionRegulated(code, profession)` — checks whether a profession is regulated in a jurisdiction.
- `findJurisdictionsForProfession(profession)` — finds all jurisdictions where a given profession is regulated.

### Age and consent

- `getDigitalConsentAge(code)`: minimum age for digital services without parental consent. Reads `childProtection.minAgeDigitalConsent` (not `dataProtection.digitalConsentAge`; equal for all 28 today, not enforced). Defaults to 16 for unknown jurisdictions.
- `getAgeOfMajority(code)` — legal age of majority. Defaults to 18 for unknown jurisdictions.

### Data transfer

- `canTransferData(from, to)`: returns `{ allowed: boolean; mechanism?: string; notes?: string }`: the transfer mechanism the dataset records for the pair. It is a lookup, not legal clearance: `allowed` is `false` only when either code is unknown (`{ allowed: false, notes: 'Unknown jurisdiction' }`) and `true` for every known pair, including `safeguards-required`.
  - `mechanism` is typed as a plain string (no exported union). Values: `domestic`, `eu-internal`, `adequacy-decision`, `mutual-recognition`, `no-restrictions`, `safeguards-required`.
  - Direction matters: rules come from the source jurisdiction (`FR` to `GB` is `adequacy-decision`, `GB` to `FR` is `safeguards-required`). First match wins: unknown code, same code (`domestic`), source has no outbound restrictions (`no-restrictions`, destination ignored; only US and CA today), both EU/EEA (`eu-internal`), EU/EEA source and destination on the EU adequacy list (`adequacy-decision`), destination in source's `mutualRecognition` list (`mutual-recognition`), otherwise `safeguards-required`.
  - `mutual-recognition` here reuses the professional credential recognition list; it is a heuristic, not evidence of a data-transfer treaty.

### Language

- `getAllLanguages()` — returns a sorted array of all language codes across jurisdictions.
- `getJurisdictionsByLanguage(lang)` — returns jurisdictions that list the given language. Case-insensitive.

### Confidence scoring

- `computeJurisdictionConfidence(code)` — returns a detailed confidence breakdown (0-100) covering professional body coverage, public register availability, digital credentials, data protection maturity, mutual recognition, e-signature, and legal system.
- `getJurisdictionConfidence(code)` — returns just the numeric confidence score.
- `rankJurisdictionsByConfidence()` — returns all jurisdictions ranked by confidence score (highest first).

### Exported data

- `JURISDICTIONS`: `Record<string, Jurisdiction>` containing all jurisdiction data. Only the top level is frozen (shallow `Object.freeze`): nested objects and arrays are mutable, and the lookup functions return those live references, so treat everything as read-only and copy before changing anything.

## Types

- `Jurisdiction` — code, name, nameLocal, legalSystem, languages, currency, professionalBodies, dataProtection, childProtection, eSignatureRecognised, mutualRecognition, notes.
- `ProfessionalBody` — id, name, nameEn, profession, website, hasPublicRegister, registerUrl, issuesDigitalCredentials, notes.
- `DataProtectionLaw`: name, fullName, year, digitalConsentAge (not read by `getDigitalConsentAge`), requiresExplicitConsent, breachNotificationHours, rightToErasure, rightToPortability, crossBorderRestrictions, maxRetentionDays, supervisoryAuthority, notes.
- `ChildProtectionLaw` — name, minAgeDigitalConsent, ageOfMajority, requiresParentalConsent, enhancedProtections, profilingRestrictions.
- `LegalSystem` — 'common-law' | 'civil-law' | 'mixed' | 'religious' | 'customary'.
- `ProfessionType` — 'legal' | 'medical' | 'notary' | 'accounting' | 'engineering' | 'teaching' | 'financial' | 'veterinary' | 'pharmacy' | 'architecture' | 'social-work'.
- `JurisdictionConfidence` — code, score, breakdown (7 sub-scores).

## Use cases

- **Legal-tech compliance** — determine which professional bodies are authorised to practise in a jurisdiction.
- **KYC jurisdictional intelligence** — look up data protection law, digital consent age, and breach notification requirements.
- **Cross-border data transfer lookup**: find the recorded transfer mechanism (GDPR adequacy decision, mutual recognition or safeguards) for a pair of jurisdictions.
- **Professional body lookups** — find regulated bodies by country and profession.
- **Age verification** — retrieve digital consent age and age of majority per jurisdiction.
- **Mutual recognition** — discover which jurisdictions have formal credential recognition agreements.
- **Jurisdiction ranking** — score and rank jurisdictions by how well they support credential verification.

## Law notes

The repository also holds written-up legal research, separate from the dataset and not shipped in the package. Each note is dated and marks every claim by how it was checked. Research, not legal advice.

- [Index and conventions](https://github.com/forgesworn/jurisdiction-kit/blob/main/law/README.md)
- [GB: running an online service](https://github.com/forgesworn/jurisdiction-kit/blob/main/law/gb/online-services.md): Online Safety Act 2023, UK GDPR, PECR, Investigatory Powers Act 2016, export control, trading rules.
- [legal-cover skill](https://github.com/forgesworn/jurisdiction-kit/blob/main/skill/SKILL.md): an agent skill for Claude Code and Codex that applies the notes to a project.

## Limits

Static data compiled in 2025 with no exact as-of date and no per-entry verification date; the EU adequacy list behind `canTransferData` is annotated as of 2024. Informational only, not legal advice. CHANGELOG.md ships in the package and dates each release.

## Install

```
npm install jurisdiction-kit
```

ESM only, with no CommonJS build: use `import`, not `require()`. The compiled output uses nothing newer than ES2020 syntax, so it runs on Node 14 or later (`engines` in `package.json` says the same); it is developed and tested on Node 24.

## Example

```typescript
import { getJurisdiction, canTransferData, getProfessionalBodies } from 'jurisdiction-kit';

const gb = getJurisdiction('GB');
if (!gb) throw new Error('GB is not in the dataset'); // Jurisdiction | undefined: narrow before use
// gb.name === 'United Kingdom'
// gb.dataProtection.name === 'UK GDPR + DPA 2018'

const transfer = canTransferData('FR', 'GB');
// transfer.allowed === true, transfer.mechanism === 'adequacy-decision'
// allowed: true means the dataset has a mechanism for the pair, not that the transfer is lawful

const lawyers = getProfessionalBodies('GB', 'legal');
// [{ name: 'The Law Society of England and Wales', ... }, ...]
```
